TO STAY AHEAD ON AI, THINK LIKE A DESIGNER https://every.


HOW TO APPLY YOUR EXPERTISE WHEN AI ABSORBS THE WORK https://every.

by Aishwarya Reganti https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVG8gU3RheSBBaGVhZCBvbiBBSSwgVGhpbmsgTGlrZSBhIERlc2lnbmVyIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDM5OSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vQGFpc2gubnIiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6M30=

Midjourney/Every illustration.

This is the final piece in our series on “unlearning,” in partnership with Maven, the expert-led course platform. First, Hilary Gridley explained why faster prototypes don’t make product decisions easier https://every.. Then, Xinran Ma shared what he unlearned after leaving corporate product design to work for himself https://every.. Former Amazon AI scientist and LevelUp Labs founder Aishwarya Reganti considers what happens when AI can do the work that once proved your expertise. She calls the next step designing the work: applying your expertise before execution begins so the people and AI agents doing it can make better decisions.—Kate Lee https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVG8gU3RheSBBaGVhZCBvbiBBSSwgVGhpbmsgTGlrZSBhIERlc2lnbmVyIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDM5OSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vQGthdGVfMTc2NyIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo2fQ==

Was this newsletter forwarded to you? Sign up https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVG8gU3RheSBBaGVhZCBvbiBBSSwgVGhpbmsgTGlrZSBhIERlc2lnbmVyIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDM5OSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vYWNjb3VudCIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo3fQ== to get it in your inbox.



----------------------------------------



These days, I call myself a designer, though I don’t design interfaces or logos. My job, instead, is to make sure the people and AI agents I work with can make the same decisions that I would. I design how the work gets done.

That would have surprised me earlier in my career, when I built my reputation on execution. Before starting my company, I did research in AI and machine learning, and then worked as an AI scientist at Amazon for six years. “Build fast, fix later” was my motto. Given a task, I completed it as quickly as I could, because the work itself was hard. Execution was proof of expertise.

But now that an AI can produce a passable version, in minutes, of what used to set us apart, the question many of us are sitting with is: If the machine does the thing I was known for, what is left?

What is on the other side of that question is more interesting than what we think we are losing. On the other side lies a sense of calm and confidence, a tailwind of capability. But getting there requires first letting go of the belief that we are what we produce.

https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVG8gU3RheSBBaGVhZCBvbiBBSSwgVGhpbmsgTGlrZSBhIERlc2lnbmVyIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDM5OSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vbGluay5zdml4LmNvbS9ldmVyeXRvIiwicG9zaXRpb24iOjh9




WIN MORE DEALS BY SHIPPING RELIABLE WEBHOOKS FOR YOUR CUSTOMERS

Your customers want their agent workflows to be event-driven, so you’re losing deals if your API lacks reliable webhooks. Webhooks lead to deeper product engagement, stronger retention, and integrated workflows, but retries, ordering, and replay protection are harder than they look. Svix authored Standard Webhooks https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVG8gU3RheSBBaGVhZCBvbiBBSSwgVGhpbmsgTGlrZSBhIERlc2lnbmVyIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDM5OSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vd3d3LnN0YW5kYXJkd2ViaG9va3MuY29tLyIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo5fQ==, the spec adopted by Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Twilio, and Etsy.

If you homebrewed your webhooks and are getting pinged at 4 in the morning for failed deliveries, this is for you. Svix handles everything: retries, idempotency, security, and compliance. Qualified startups get $12,000 in free credits—$50,000 if you’re a YC company.

Get started for free https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVG8gU3RheSBBaGVhZCBvbiBBSSwgVGhpbmsgTGlrZSBhIERlc2lnbmVyIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDM5OSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vbGluay5zdml4LmNvbS9ldmVyeXRvP3NvdXJjZT1wb3N0X2J1dHRvbiIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjoxMH0=
Want to sponsor Every? Click here https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVG8gU3RheSBBaGVhZCBvbiBBSSwgVGhpbmsgTGlrZSBhIERlc2lnbmVyIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDM5OSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Im1haWx0bzpzcG9uc29yc2hpcHNAZXZlcnkudG8iLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6MTF9.


THE WORLD WE WERE TRAINED FOR

School rewarded execution. You were graded on the essays you wrote and the projects you turned in on time. Careers rewarded it the same way. Performance reviews measured output, and promotions often went to those who produced the most, the fastest, at the highest quality.

At first, AI seems like a boon to someone who grew up this way. If I’m doing X, then I should be able to do it much better, and much faster, with AI augmenting me. This leads you to chase every new tool and technique, because even incremental improvements are still improvements.

But the next thing is just around the corner. Fine-tuning an AI model using smaller, specialized data sets was “the thing” for maybe eight months before retrieval augmented generation https://every.

by Mike Taylor https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIEJlc3QgQUkgQWdlbnQgQnVpbGRlciBJcyBUcmFwcGVkIEluc2lkZSBNaWNyb3NvZnQiLCJwb3N0X2lkIjo0Mzk3LCJwb3N0X3R5cGUiOiJwcm9tbyIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vQG1pa2VfMjExNCIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo0fQ==

This is a free preview of a subscribers-only post.

----------------------------------------



I’ve taught AI workshops to thousands of people, and the most common reason people give me for using Microsoft Copilot over Claude or ChatGPT is “because I have to.”

Much like Teams over Slack, or SharePoint over Drive, corporate IT departments choose Copilot because it’s the safe option that integrates with all the other ones Microsoft has supplied you over the years.

Meanwhile all the fun is being had elsewhere. In the nine months from May 2025 to February 2026, Claude Code became the most popular AI coding tool, with 63 percent of respondents reaching for it in Pragmatic Engineer’s survey https://every.. Microsoft-owned GitHub Copilot https://every. lost the lead in a category it invented when it launched in 2021, a year and a half before the release of ChatGPT-3.

More recently, Codex usage shot up from 6 million to 10 million users https://every. in a week, as its new GPT-5.6 Sol https://every. model and lingering uncertainty over Anthropic’s Fable access https://every. convinced people to switch. As Dan Shipper https://every. noticed early https://every., the Codex app had been building momentum for six months before the latest model tipped the scales.

Something similar is happening with Copilot Studio. I’m not talking about GitHub Copilot or the Copilot app (more on that later). I’m talking about Microsoft’s no-code platform for creating AI agents. It’s similar to OpenAI’s custom GPTs, crossed with Microsoft Power Platform—a trio of pre-AI low-code/no-code business tools featuring Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power BI. You build custom workflows that wire your data connectors into AI agents.

Since I work with a lot of financial services firms and large companies, I have the distinction of being the first person at Every to buy a Copilot license. An IT leader working for one of my clients showed me the AI agents he built with the tool and told me, “People don’t realize that Microsoft has become the best place for us to do this.”

That got me excited enough to cover Microsoft Build https://every. and line up an interview with Ryan Cunningham, corporate vice president of Copilot Studio, about how the company arrived here.

I’m convinced Microsoft has a shot at making the best tools to build AI agents people actually use. We may be only one confusing administrative provisioni

#### **THROUGH THE VALLEY**

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/72178c36-8182-474d-a723-819df8018189/geminirobotics2-featured__1_.png?t=1785768037)
Caption: Courtesy: Google DeepMind

**1/ OpenAI's next model solved decades-old math problems:** OpenAI revealed that [Astra](https://x.com/polynoamial/status/2083467194663571701?s=20), an internal version of its next major model family, [solved](https://openai.com/index/ten-advances-in-mathematics) 10 long open problems across mathematics and computer science, including some that had remained unsolved for nearly 30 years. The proofs were formally verified in Lean and cost roughly $2,000 in API tokens to generate, and reports suggest Astra could launch as GPT-5.7, GPT-6, or under a new brand with more advanced versions released under restricted access.

**2/ Alibaba launches its most powerful AI model yet:** Alibaba unveiled [Qwen3.8-Max](https://x.com/Alibaba_Qwen/status/2084100707423289643?s=20), a 2.4 trillion parameter multimodal model built for coding, research, long-horizon agent tasks, and visual reasoning. The model supports a 1 million token context window, reportedly performs on par with Anthropic's Fable 5 in several benchmarks, and is designed to handle complex workloads with minimal human input. DeepSeek also released V4-Flash, an ultra-low-cost model estimated to be more than 100 times cheaper to run than Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.

**3/ Google gives humanoid robots full-body AI control:** Google DeepMind introduced [Gemini Robotics 2](https://deepmind.google/blog/gemini-robotics-2-brings-whole-body-intelligence-to-robots), a new AI model that controls an entire humanoid robot instead of just its arms, enabling coordinated movements like walking, crouching, reaching, and handling objects. The system can also plan complex tasks, coordinate multiple robots, run locally without constant internet access, and includes new safety features, though it remains a research project with no public release date. ([watch the demo here](https://deepmind.google/blog/gemini-robotics-2-brings-whole-body-intelligence-to-robots))

**4/ Meta plans to spend up to $145B on AI infrastructure:** Mark Zuckerberg says Meta will spend up to [$145 billion](https://siliconangle.com/2026/07/28/meta-build-14b-el-paso-data-center-campus-blackrock) on AI infrastructure in 2026, including a new 1-gigawatt Texas data center, as the company races to build an agent-first internet. Meta plans to bring persistent AI assistants to WhatsApp and Messenger, while also expanding enterprise AI tools and updating its smart glasses with new privacy protections.


----------

----------

* [AI YC Interview with Gstack Agents](https://gstack-meeting.com/) > AI interview specialists join your Google Meet, conduct YC style mock interviews, and give real time feedback on your answers

* [Coast](https://coast.app/) > A fully local memory layer for you and your AI agents, built from everything you see and do on your Mac

* [HeyGen Video Podcast](https://app.heygen.com/apps/video-podcast) > Turn a document, link, or idea into a fully produced two host video podcast with scenes, camera cuts, and B-roll

* [Claude Overlay](https://github.com/shengyanlin/claude-overlay) > It provides a floating desktop window that reads your screen and runs Claude Code tasks directly

* [Superlinear](https://superlinear.fm/) > Learn four practical agent engineering habits through a free video course and podcast series

* [Motion in Claude](https://x.com/motion_so/status/2083992227114520576?s=20) > Paste a product URL and Claude creates a complete launch video with a script, voiceover, editing, and final render

* [Dreamina Seedance 2.5](https://x.com/BytePlusGlobal/status/2083069262969844158) > BytePlus has launched its new cinematic AI video model for generating high quality videos

* [Gemini Spark](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-app/gemini-spark-updates-july-2026/) > Google's personal AI agent now integrates directly with Chrome for in browser assistance

* [Qwen3.8-Max](https://www.qwencloud.com/models/qwen3.8-max) > Alibaba's latest flagship reasoning model can code autonomously for more than 10 days


----------

----------

--------------------

TL;DR: Our new guide, “Build Faster With Voice,” shows you how to turn raw speech into finished work with AI agents. Join us on Friday, August 7, for Voice Mode Camp https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIERlZmluaXRpdmUgR3VpZGUgdG8gVXNpbmcgVm9pY2UgV2l0aCBBSSIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQzOTUsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL2V2ZW50cy92b2ljZS1tb2RlLWNhbXAiLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6NX0=, a one-hour live session where the Every team will demo practical voice workflows for writing and agent orchestration, help you get started, and answer your questions.—Kate Lee https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIERlZmluaXRpdmUgR3VpZGUgdG8gVXNpbmcgVm9pY2UgV2l0aCBBSSIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQzOTUsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL0BrYXRlXzE3NjciLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6Nn0=

----------------------------------------



Most knowledge work still starts with an act of translation. You finish a customer call and turn it into a bug report. You think through a story idea on a walk, then wait until you’re back at your laptop to organize it. Before the real work can begin, you’ve already spent time cleaning up the context.

Paired with an AI agent, voice can remove that intermediate step. You can speak while the details are fresh https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIERlZmluaXRpdmUgR3VpZGUgdG8gVXNpbmcgVm9pY2UgV2l0aCBBSSIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQzOTUsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL3d3dy5tb25vbG9ndWUudG8iLCJwb3NpdGlvbiI6OH0=, point the agent toward the relevant transcripts, code, documents, or messages, define the outcome you want, and review what it produces.

A useful way to start is with a five-step loop:

Capture → retrieve and ground → define the outcome → act → review and redirect

Today we’re publishing “Build Faster With Voice,” https://every.to/emails/click/1eb47536f45a3508ca723b5b2cb780e942839f966e324ef3162cd49469aec49f/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIERlZmluaXRpdmUgR3VpZGUgdG8gVXNpbmcgVm9pY2UgV2l0aCBBSSIsInBvc3RfaWQiOjQzOTUsInBvc3RfdHlwZSI6InBvc3QiLCJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2V2ZXJ5LnRvL2d1aWRlcy9idWlsZC1mYXN0ZXItd2l0aC12b2ljZSIsInBvc2l0aW9uIjo5fQ== a practical guide to using that loop across writing, planning, software, communication, and ongoing memory systems.

The full guide is available to paid and All Access Every members. It includes:

 * More than a dozen workflows based on how people at Every use voice with agents
 * Copyable prompts for turning recordings into article outlines, project plans, bug patches, emails, meeting follow-ups, and more
 * Setup instructions for connecting your notes and transcripts to Codex or Claude
 * The context, safeguards, and review steps each workflow needs

If you’re reading Every for free, the five-step loop above is yours to try. To get the complete prompts, setup instructions, and workflow library, you’ll need to upgrade to a paid Every subscription.

Voice doesn’t eliminate the need for good sources or careful review. Agents still need access to the material that has the final say, and consequential actions should still require your approval. The advantage is that you no longer have to turn every messy thought into polished instructions before the work can start.
